Hon'ble Manoj Bajaj,J.
Applicant has approached this Court through this application under Section 482 Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing of the proceeding of S.T. No.975 of 2016 titled as State Vs. Lalit Kumar,
arising out of Case Crime No. 670 of 2016, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Pocso Act, Police Station Kakori, District Lucknow pending before Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (Pocso Act)-I, Lucknow.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (Pocso Act)-I, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant while referring to the grounds raised in this application has submitted that the prosecution of applicant is apparently misuse of the process of law, therefore,
interference is warranted by this Court by exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 CrPC.
He prays that the proceedings of aforesaid Sessions Trial, be quashed, in the interest of justice.

During the course of hearing, it is not disputed by learned counsel that the offences contained in the FIR as well as in the impugned final report relate to the offences against human body and the case of Lalit @ Lalit Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. ...

entities.text: Lalit @ Lalit Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Deptt
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the prosecution is based upon the evidence of injured/victim.
Apart from this, it is also fairly stated by learned counsel that the impugned final report has not yet been considered by the trial court, as the charges against the accused have not been framed.

After hearing the learned counsel, this Court finds that concededly the final report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. is yet to be considered by the trial court as the charges against the applicants have not been framed so far, therefore, keeping in view of the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Dharmatma Singh vs. Harminder Singh & Ors. passed in Criminal Appeal No.1126 of 2011 (3) RCR Criminal 38, this Court is of the considered opinion that the grounds raised by the applicants herein can also be pressed before the trial court at an appropriate stage.

entities.text: Dharmatma Singh vs. Harminder Singh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Criminal Appeal No.1126 of 2011 (3) RCR Criminal 38
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Resultantly, without meaning any expression of opinion on the merits of this case, no case is made out for interference by way of exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
However, it shall be open for the applicant to raise all the grounds pleaded in this application, before the trial court at the stage of consideration of final report.
The application fails and is hereby, dismissed.

Order Date :- 9.1.2025.
